topic: Oren-Nayar V-cavity rough diffuse retroreflection vs Lambert limb darkening rig
topic_zh: Oren-Nayar 粗糙V型微槽漫反射逆反射对比朴素朗伯余弦满月与陶土边缘变暗
scope: Deterministic Michael Oren & Shree Nayar (SIGGRAPH 1994) V-cavity rough diffuse retroreflection (L_ON(theta) = cos(theta) + (B/A)*sin(theta)*tan(theta)*cos(theta) = cos(theta) + (2/3)*sin^2(theta)) versus naive Lambertian cosine falloff (cos(theta)) and 64-facet V-cavity quadrature across 17 spherical limb angles (theta in [0 deg, 80 deg]).

protocol.function: L_ON(θ) = cos θ + ⅔·sin²θ → 60° Limb = 0.5000 + 0.5000 = 1.0000 vs Lambert cos 60° = 0.5000 (−50.00% Darkened)

robustness.name: Sampled 17 spherical limb stations preserve flat full-moon and terracotta clay brightness without cosine rim darkening

good_fit: Lunar regolith, terracotta pottery, dry sand, concrete, plaster, and matte chalk in Blender, OpenPBR, MaterialX, and Three.js
Canceling the cos(theta) foreshortening drop with V-cavity retroreflection sin(theta)*tan(theta)*cos(theta) = sin^2(theta)
Locking 60° limb brightness at L_ON(60°) = 1.0000 to eliminate the -50.00% dark rim of naive Lambertian spheres
Evaluating mu + (B/A)*(1 - mu^2) in 3 algebraic operations from dot(N, V) without trig calls
not_for: Mirror-smooth polished metals or glossy plastics dominated by specular BRDF lobes
Subsurface translucent wax or skin where photons diffuse across millimeters (use Christensen-Burley Round 108)
Refractive dielectric glass (use Walter Rough Refraction BTDF Round 109)
